turns.text: I just tipped a pan of boiling water over my forearm — the skin's red and blistering. What's the correct first aid right now?
Why is cool running water the treatment and for so long? What's it doing?
What should I cover it with afterwards, and should I leave the blisters alone?
If I rang a nurse line, what would they want to know about the burn's size and depth?
What do burns nurses say about ointments and creams in the first days?
A friend says cling film loosely over it is what they use in hospitals. Is that right?
Someone else told me to take off my watch and rings straight away. Why?
The nearest clinic is closed till Monday and I'm in agony. What painkillers help, and how do I sleep with it?
Which signs over the weekend mean I go to the emergency department instead of waiting?
Could you give me a plan — first aid now, covering, painkillers, care over the weekend, and when to get seen?
